## Natural history notes

A medium-sized flower fly characterized by a bee-like body, dark-and-yellow bicolored patterning, large eyes, and hovering flight around flowers. In Florida, the Bicolored Plushback is found in warm gardens, parks, hammocks, forest edges, roadsides, and other flower-rich habitats, with records extending through Florida as part of its tropical-to-southern U.S. range. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen and can act as pollinators, while the larvae of related Palpada hover flies are typically aquatic or semi-aquatic filter-feeders in wet, decaying organic material, helping recycle nutrients in small wet microhabitats.
